question:
Show that the area of the triangle with vertices $A(x_1, y_1)$, $B(x_2, y_2)$, $C(x_3, y_3)$ is given by:

$\displaystyle \frac{1}{2} \left| \begin{matrix} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \end{matrix} \right|$ using determinants.
explanation:
The area $\Delta$ of triangle $ABC$ with vertices $A(x_1, y_1)$, $B(x_2, y_2)$ and $C(x_3, y_3)$ is:

$\Delta = \frac{1}{2} |x_1(y_2 - y_3) + x_2(y_3 - y_1) + x_3(y_1 - y_2)|$

But we can write this with determinants:

$= \frac{1}{2} \left| \begin{array}{ccc} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \end{array} \right|$

Let's expand the determinant to check:

$\left| \begin{array}{ccc} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \end{array} \right| = x_1(y_2 \cdot 1 - y_3 \cdot 1) - y_1(x_2 \cdot 1 - x_3 \cdot 1) + 1(x_2 y_3 - x_3 y_2)$

$= x_1(y_2 - y_3) - y_1(x_2 - x_3) + x_2 y_3 - x_3 y_2$

After rearrangement and substituting appropriately, it gives exactly the area formula above.

Hence proved.
